Red Faction Armageddon is a suprisingly good game that unfortunately saw only tepid performance in the marketplace.  The DirectX 11 visuals, physics engine, wide variety of weapons as well as a multiplayer/co-op mode make for a solid third person shooter. Armageddon is a sub-par game at best, and it struggles to hold a candle to Guerilla, its predecessor. While it certainly gets a bit more inventive with its arsenal, Armageddon has regressed into an ultra-linear shooter that's fundamentally far less enjoyable to play. It suffers from boring levels, repetitive encounters, an excess of vehicle/on-rails sections, and more.

There are some improvements in regards to your arsenal. Ammo is far more abundant in comparison to Guerilla and there are more gimmicky or niche weapons. The maul is no longer mandatory and can be swapped out at will. You now possess a magnet gun, which has infinite ammo and can easily obliterate enemies and buildings. Other funky new inclusions are weapons such as the singularity cannon, the plasma cannon (which is basically the Doom 3 BFG), and the pulse mine (which does no damage to the environment). The assault rifle is pretty viable in this game and stayed a part of my arsenal for most of the game.

There's some bizarre problems with movement in this game. The game frequently eats your inputs when you try to sprint or dodge, which is incredibly obnoxious. The magnet gun has some serious problems with eating inputs as well. For whatever reason, the game sometimes decides to delete your bolts or prevent you from firing it. Sometimes, rather unpredictably, you can get stunned or ragdolled. I'm generally not sure what causes you to get stunned, but it prevents you from firing or moving for a brief moment. Getting ragdolled completely prevents movement. Getting ragdolled is predictable, but it makes melee encounters obnoxious. You can easily get combo'd to death if the game decides that it hates you.

Enemy design is a super mixed bag. Humans are only encountered a handful of times throughout the game, which means you'll be fighting the new aliens for majority of the game. Unfortunately, these aliens only have a handful of types and most of them are incredibly damage spongy. They magically teleport all over the place and often come from spawners that will spawn them endlessly. You can destroy objects so that they can't climb or jump around, but this often takes more effort than just outright killing them. The largest aliens, the behemoths, are the worst by far, as they have enough health to exhaust the entire ammo capacity of multiple power weapons. This game never mixes enemies up intelligently, especially near the end. I'm not even sure if most late-game encounters would be remotely possible (on the hardest difficulty) without the infinite ammo granted by the berserk ability.

Level design is often absolute garbage. Destructible environments aren't used in very compelling ways. The game doesn't hesitate to put you on a paper-thin bridge above a death pit, where a slight breeze will completely annihilate the bridge. Even when I felt like I was making intelligent use of the environment, it was never clear how effective it really was. I made an entire water tower collapse on a mini-boss, but it barely did any damage to it. There's also an overload of turret and vehicle segments in this game. Some of these turret/on-rails segments are astoundingly awful, as you'll be swarmed from a long distance away with no ability to take cover or properly move around. Vehicles are generally extremely slow and turn awkwardly, and each vehicle you pilot is worse than the last.

There's a couple other miscellaneous problems that I have with this game as well. While the ability to rebuild structures is nice, it's generally niche outside of level progression. Only a couple times throughout the whole game did I use it tactically or for exploration. There's no jetpack in this game, which is rather unfortunate. As a result, this game has less verticality than Guerilla did. The abilities you can activate are rather overpowered in general. They tend to recharge quickly and the late-game forces you to use them almost non-stop. You have little reason to not constantly berserk for a massive damage boost and bottomless magazines. I feel like this would be cool in most other games, but enemies are so spongy that exploiting infinite ammo is almost mandatory.

This game is truly something. I started off liking it, but quickly started to hate many aspects of it. Even though the environmental destruction was impressive (whenever the developers remembered it's a feature, at least), nothing else about the game was impressive in the same way. It's ultimately this substandard TPS with obnoxious enemy design and forgettable level design that keeps going on and on. I really can't recommend this. Just play Guerilla instead.

I've replayed this game 3 or 4 times now. First time was on console, second on PC. I disliked (and even hated) it because it wasn't an open world sandbox like guerrilla.

Now after my most recent playthrough I finally see it for what it is. It succeeds in all the ways guerrilla didn't. The story is okay, maybe even good. But the mechanics are a direct evolution of guerrilla's.
The abilities added by the nanoforge and its ability to repair really add more variety to the combat and how you approach the game. Not being forced to use the hammer and instead take a 4th weapon also helps give you more options, with the more powerful melee and abilities compensating for its loss if you decide not to use it.

The level design is great considering how much of it is destructible and how the game is still designed with that in mind.
The only real bad points I can really talk about are that whilst the game runs fine, its missing an FOV option. This is absolutely critical in making the game not feel like a bad console port. If you buy this game please go to https://community.pcgamingwiki.com/files/file/421-red-faction-armageddon-fov-fix/ and download a better fox option. This improves the game so much its essential imo, even on console the over the shoulder view felt to close (especially if you where coming straight from Guerrilla).
Other than that there's also a weird issue with the spider walkers aiming controls in the few parts of the game you drive them. It's easy enough to just power through it though.

The games style definitely feels a bit weird compared to guerrilla but this is something that's more down to personal preference, and doesn't really affect the gameplay beyond some of the weapons feeling radically different is all.

Ultimately, it would be amazing if the next red faction game could take the best bits of Armageddon and combine them with the best bits of Guerrilla. Guerrilla's weak points where pretty much just its story and missions being kind of meh, being mostly held up by just its unique destruction mechanics, where as Armageddon fixes these issues, but its linier gameplay feels like a step back for the series. I really feel like a mix of both could make for a near perfect game if done right. It's sad that something like this has so little hope of happening now ;-;

Rating: 7/10 without taking technical issues into account, with them: 3/10.

Unlike the beloved previous entry, Guerilla with its open map and non-linear (for the most part) progression, Armageddon is a linear shooter, mostly set in the caverns of Mars - much like the almost forgotten first two games in the series. As such, it received a lot of undue hate from the new fans, whose first game of the series was the above-mentioned open-world entry. I have been disappointed by that as well, but as I played the first two games, not as much.

The game itself, when not applying the expectations from Guerilla, is pretty good fit into the series. It has solid graphics, solid gunplay, and the semi-destructive environment with a couple new twists. The story - including interaction between characters, much like in most shooters of this type, is B/C-grade action movie cringefest [spoiler] you fuck up and cause two terrible things resulting in deaths of thousands, people hate you, but you do everything to save them, while fighting through 6 gazillion enemies like the hero you are [/spoiler], which also fits overall into the series. However, the envirnoments are pretty cool, and the enemies are also interesting with a decent variety of abilities, as is the selection of weapons, which makes up for crappy story - after all, a shooter is made up by what you shoot with what gun more so than why you shoot.

The sound design is also pretty good for the most part, though some weapons could use a bit beefier sound. The soundtrack is also pretty good, especially in some of the horror-lite sections of the game.

Armageddon also plays pretty well, I have a pretty low-end PC as I generally play older games, an i3-4160 and a GT-1030, with 16 gigs of ram and a SSD, and the game plays pretty smoothly on everything turned up to max, including 8x MSAA and 16x AF, except for a couple instances with a lot of destruction and a lot of enemies on screen, where the game did dip under 30 a bit.

However, the game falls flat in one regard: The game will crash every 2nd-3rd time you get to a checkpoint in a session when in DX10/11 mode (so generally every 20 minutes), and will crash every hour or so in DX9 mode. The graphical difference is pretty minor, so if you absolutely have to play the game, you can do so in DX9 and get through it with about 6-12 crashes (depending on whether you rush through or take your time exploring and getting all of the stuff the game offers (guns and upgrades)). However, this is pretty unacceptable, at least for me, so I cannot recommend buying the game, unless you can get it for really low price - I paid around 1.89 EUR for it IIRC, I cannot endorse paying more than that for it, especially since the chances of the dev. team releasing a patch for it are literally non-existent.

Alternatively, I would recommend getting this game on console, if you own one. You will suffer a bit in regards to graphical fidelity and perhaps framerate, but you will not have to restart the game every 15-60 minutes.

I don't understand the negative reviews for this game(barring the ones talking about crashes and instability, the game only crashed for me once). This is a pretty good game, considering the series and, honestly, I think this might be the best of the entire series, as ridiculous as that might sound to some people.

Let's begin with a history lesson, because I think some of the negative reviews don't understand where this series come from. The first two Red Faction games are, and let's be honest here, Half Life clones. There's no getting around it. Sure, they have their own unique individual twists on run-and-gunning, and "puzzles" but if you were to play both those games, the experience is very much similar outside of small unique differences. The stories are also really boring at the core. Then comes along Red Faction Guerrilla, a game that boasts a ton of destruction and a pretty damn good physics engine for the time. Story was pretty good and was an expansion on Red Faction 1's story, not 2(2 doesn't even take place on Mars?). So, if you look at the Red Faction series, this game is a huge departure from the previous game for many reasons, but I think for the better overall.

The story starts with you, the son of the man from the previous game(I guess? The stories of all the games always slip away from me), trying to stop some mad cultist, that really hates your family for some reason, from destroying the Mars Terraformer. The Mars Terraformer, in which there is only one for some reason, gets destroyed and now everyone has to go underground to survive, although humans can still go above ground, the weather is just *really* bad. What secrets are hidden underground? Who knows, you'll probably find out soon though. This game's story takes on a much more horror theme compared to previous and I think this is what turned off most people who played it, but the atmosphere and the story is pretty decent, it's straight forward, and it's fun. 

The gameplay is pretty good but be warned that you are in fact getting a mediocre 3rd-person shooter. It's pretty consistent and balanced but it gets boring and annoying eventually. Specifically, the enemies you fight the most can cling to walls and they jump around *a lot*. They're not hard to kill, they're just hard to pin down. There is a decent variety of enemies, however, and to top it off there are bosses and they are pretty cool to fight. There's a decent variety of weapons too and seeing the destruction in this game may be limited because you're underground most of the time but when you do get a chance to use the different weapons, it is very fun and cool to see. Overall, a pretty fun game to play and the destruction factor is decent in this game. Also, I saw another review say this game can be up to 20 hours long... not even close. I completed this game in the hours you see here. 7.8 hours. Very short game but it was fun. Honestly, the worst thing I can say about this game is that it's too short and it feels rushed. Also, it isn't the most stable and it crashes sometimes.

I get the impression players wanted more of Guerrilla, and I get it... but do you really want the same game over and over? This is something that ruins most game series because of the hilariously self-destructive nerd rage some nerd-gamers have. Will we ever see another Red Faction game? I doubt it as THQ reportedly pulled the plug on the series after this game because it sold so badly and, honestly? I most blame the "fans". I'm sure they were working with what they got.

Speaking on Red Faction Guerrilla, it wasn't even that great of a game story-wise and the gameplay was mostly fun in the destruction factor but the gunplay sucked, the open world aspect was mediocre, and you could straight up permanently miss out on side mission / objectives in the game if you don't know you have to complete them before progressing in the story, and that's just the surface of the issues I personally had with the game.

Get this game if you want a decent action game with *some* destruction physics. I wouldn't buy it if you're expecting another Red Faction Guerrilla.

Having played through all of the Red Factions this week, Armageddon is my second favorite game in the series. I personally wasn't a huge fan of the open world or story telling in Guerrilla as I found it kind of empty and bland, though the destruction and gameplay loop in Guerrilla was a blast. This game, even nine years after its release, still looks fantastic with the settings maxed out. 

It goes back to one of the major themes from the original game, and tries to expand a bit on what Capek was working on. It is a strong installment to the series and it's a shame that the series was pretty much killed off, hopefully someday we'll have a reboot.

An additional effect aside from the destruction the series has become known for is reconstruction enabling you, for example, to completely destroy a bridge during combat that's needed for level progression and later allowing you to rebuild it.  

On the downside, from a PC perspective the FOV is too close and I've never really adjusted.  To compensate I've moved to a couch/plasma/cont setup so that I'm farther back from the screen.  While this improves the expereince it's not optimal.  On the upside the DX11 visuals are great given the console nature of the game.  The story is good enough though it takes time to develop.

Other than the fact the game crashes at every single checkpoint in the game, the game is a lot of fun and looks great.. Once the game crashes at the checkpoint, you can go to that checkpoint and beyond, it will crash again at the next checkpoint and the next and the next, you just need start at the last checkpoint.  It's annoying but at least the game is playable.

I'll say I don't hate on games. I may have a love-hate relationship with some games and come back every so often; and others that I drop. However I feel that this one really dropped the ball for it's PC (Or at least Steam) port. Why? Why is it so? The Xbox 360 port was perfect.

This one however has so many issues. Did you click continue or load a save? Sorry, we have to boot you back to the main screen until the button does it's job. Did you step, jump or turn around 1% [i]too fast?[/i] I guess the game has to hard crash on you. Now you have to play it in windowed mode and set it up like that every single time you boot up the game. That and have the task manager on standby in case it happens again. Oh and don't bother playing Infection then play the story, then it [i]always[/i] boots you.

Now that the technical stuff is out of the way we can move on to the gameplay. It's a downgrade from not just Guerrilla but also the original that was also underground. Enemies jump whenever they feel like it from one surface to another which if it were not for the auto-aim be a pain to actually shoot. Let's also not forget that you have regenerating health and the majority of enemies deal chip damage that will reset how much time you will have to wait to regen. Then there's the fact that all the other enemies that don't deal chip damage are tanks that will suck up most of your (Albeit plentiful) ammo every single time you encounter one of them.

Most cave missions have a very samey look to them making it annoying to get around with all the aliens shooting tic-tacs at you that respawn quicker than babies are born. Then there's the last few sections of the game that have all of the above crammed into one very long, very annoying and agonizing drag through the alien hive.

Oh yeah and the story, it's nothing to write home about like with a lot of Volition titles. Suffice to say Red Faction: Guerrilla was the peak of it's series and Red Faction: Armageddon was the series tumbling down the other side of that mountain never to be seen or talked about ever again. And that's a shame because I really, [b]really[/b] liked Guerrilla as a kid. And this too. If you are buying it just get the achievements and never go back for anything else. 4/10, it was fun while it lasted.

Red Faction Armageddon is a third person rail shooter, and even if i'm not a fan nor a vet of the gerne i really enjoyed it.

The narrative is actually good enough, surely the plot is not amazing in itsef, but thanks to a good mix of badass, funny (thanks S.A.M.) and dramatic (in particular THAT dramatic moment) well written lines and moments it really becomes a very pleasant experience, (the absence of secondary quests or other errands which could break the "flow" of the main story may also be a plus in this regard). Most levels also have a very good atmospheric feeling.

The gameplay is very solid, you have bunch of very different weapons at your disposal (the magnet gun, you never grow tired of that:), plus the distruction mechanics (i think is the best i've seen in a game so far) really let you solve the various challenges you have to face with different approaches, also boosting replay value. Also a nice character progression is implemeted and you may upgrade Darius' gear and abilities proceding in the game.

On the technical side graphics are very good, in particular the explosion looks gorgeous, and the performance were fine. I've not expereinced any glitch, bug or crash (but other rewiers instead did).

Once you finish the story you have a story+ option that let you replay it with all your upgrades and special weapons (ever dreamed of disintegrating your enemy with a rainbow ray coming out from a pony's ass? I didnt but whatever) unlocked from the start.
There are also a singleplayer destruction mode that can be a lot of fun and a very good multiplayer coop survival mode (even if recently might be hard to find players online).

Conclusion: I really enjoyed this game (completed the main story 2 times and i'll probably come back for more sooner or later) and i surely raccomend it to anyone which is interested in pleasant, linear, story-driven shooter experience.

Red Faction: Armageddon is an action packed third person shooter which follows up from the previous Red Faction: Guerrilla game and continues the Red Faction story line. However, this time the game sticks with the third person view from Guerrilla and also drops the open world concept and is linear like the first original two games. The storyline and missions are still fun as ever and works out well even though the amazing open world from Guerrilla is gone. The gameplay is pretty standard, but lots of fun and you also have a new nifty magnet gun and some powers with the Nano Forge which sometimes make you feel like a superhero or a Jedi. Once again the highlight of the Red Faction series is blowing stuff up, and you can blow up all the structures and also repair things since enemies will often be attacking you and stairs and other things you need to access will be gone. Lastly, there's an Infestion (Horde) mode which is tons of fun where you have to stay alive and fend off all of the enemies. Overall, this game is a lot of fun and is not like the previous game, however for what it is - you'll have a blast playing by blowing things up and fighting off evil cultist and aliens. I spent around 12 hours beating the story and also the DLC campaign (super short) and playing around in Infestion mode.

Note: If your game crashes during checkpoints in DX10/11 Mode, turn Shadows OFF. This worked for me and the game never crashed again since I did this.

Reminds me of Fallout 4 in a way:
Good game in general. Bad Red Faction game.


[b]The Good[/b]
1. Audio: Music/Soundtrack, Sound FX, Voice acting
2. Visuals: Art style/direction, Creature/Vehicle/Armor/Weapon designs
3. Gameplay: Gunplay, Movement, Powers, Destructible environment (limited in what can be destroyed, but very satisfying), along with a Re-construction power. Some of the physics-manipulating weapons are amazing.
4. Variety/Replay Value: Upgrade system, along with a large selection of weapons and a moderate selection of powers would allow for about 3 distinct play-styles/play-throughs (although the story is linear, and so it would be a once-a-year endeavor). Moderately large amount of enemies
5. Writing/Characters/Setting: Although the setting and main villain are just okay, most of the writing was very engaging. The 3 main protagonists had me rooting for them [spoiler]and often surprised me with how competent and active they were in the story, even when off-screen[/spoiler]. 
6. Difficulty: Medium difficulty setting was a good time.
7. Pacing and Length: Even with a few rough spots in the writing/gameplay/technical issues, the strong pacing and variety helped smooth over these rough edges. Story doesn't overstay its welcome.

[b]The Bad[/b]
1. Bugs: During cut-scene/transitions, my game would often bring up the pause menu without my input, including when I would close the pause menu, only to have it pop right back up. I think I had one freeze that required a restart, but am not sure.
2. Ending: Gameplay-wise, the ending felt a bit underwhelming, though the story was fine.
3. Antagonist/Villain is unbelievable.
4. High Fantasy/Plot Armor: I don't like either. Having the grounded characters/dialogue/setting(half of it)/ tone clashing with most of the main characters' plot armor and high-octane-over-the-top action sequences moderately bothered me many times throughout my 10 hour play-through, but the pacing usually re-engaged me quickly after each instance. Like the Fallout series, or Rick and Morty, Armageddon doesn't take itself too seriously but serious enough for the roller-coaster theme park comedy-drama to be effective at the key points.
5. Originality: it's not. You'll have seen this story, these characters, these abilities, these gameplay systems/mechanics done before and generally better in other games. It is charming and fun in spite of this.
